issues.description: Class field identifiers in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java are declared using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the problem specification (problem_statement.md UML and attribute list) and the rest of the solution class (constructor, getters/setters, toString and other methods) use camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). This mismatch causes the solution to be non-compilable (constructor and methods reference undefined camelCase fields) and will confuse students attempting to map the UML/spec to the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make identifier naming consistent between the UML/spec and the solution implementation. Recommended fix: rename the declared fields in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) so they match the constructor, getters/setters and methods. Alternatively (less recommended), update all constructor and method references to use the snake_case field names. After renaming, ensure the constructor assignments, all getters/setters, toString(), and other methods reference the same field identifiers and that the file compiles.
